outcome.shown: A hash map is a data structure that implements an associative array, allowing for efficient data retrieval by mapping unique keys to specific values. It works by using a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets or slots, from which the desired value can be found. Because the hash function provides direct access to the memory location based on the key, hash maps typically offer average-case constant time complexity, O(1), for search, insertion, and deletion operations, making them an essential tool for high-performance data management.
